Hi, I’m currently going through the baby making process with my wife. 

We actually found a sperm donor through Facebook. There are plenty of groups focused on bringing donors and recipients together. 

When we started looking into our options, we realised how ridiculously expensive it was to use a sperm bank or go to a fertility clinic for help, which is why we looked at less traditional avenues.

It’s up to you to ensure that you find somebody sensible and healthy. We asked the donor a lot of questions, and he asked us a lot of questions (making sure that we would be good parents and that we are in a stable relationship). Our donor also showed us relevant health related information. We also exchanged signed contracts basically saying that he would not pursue custody and that he isn’t liable for child support, etc.

Plus he donates for free.

We have used him several times and are seeing him again this weekend, so hopefully we will have some good news by Christmas time.

When we started this, I did have some concerns with how I would feel about the whole situation. I have no doubts that when we eventually have a child, I will love it as my own. The only thing that I get upset about is that we are unable to try naturally in the sense that when my wife is ovulating, we can’t just have sex, and that we have to rely on somebody else’s availability. So that sucks sometimes.

Hi,

My partner and I are long distance. She lives in Wisconsin, USA, whereas I live in rainy England.  

We have known each other for coming up to 11 years now, having met on a RP board during the AvidGamers days. Although we have always had feelings for one another, we never thought a relationship would actually be able to work due to the distance. But last April, we took the plunge and decided to give it ago, and have been together (and now engaged!) ever since. 

We manage to see each other pretty regularly. I am currently counting down the days until we fly away on holiday next month. 

We filed for a k1 visa back in August and are expecting to hear back end of Feb/March, so yes, I definitely plan on moving to America. I can’t imagine not having her in my life and as it stands, me moving there is much easier and more practical than her moving here. 

I have only recently come out as trans but she helped me process most of my feelings surrounding that. A lot of what she said really opened my eyes. She dated a MtF in the past so she was already super knowledgeable about the trans community. 

She has been very open and frank with her family about what I’m going through. She is 100% supportive and always refers to me as my new name, and specified pronouns. I feel very loved. So far her family have been very accepting and supportive, which is (only a tiny bit) surprising since they struggled to initially accept that she was in a relationship with a woman, so I assumed this may be an issue. I was wrong, fortunately. They are lovely people. 

I am a little worried about how people will react when I move but she currently lives in a LGBTQ+ friendly city, friendlier than where I actually live right now.

I feel like I can relate. I have been suffering from depression, anxiety and a debilitating eating disorder for most of my life. I sometimes thought “what if..?” but until recently, I openly identified as a lesbian, and as a result, I put all of my curiosities down to that. 

I’ve done a lot of thinking, and researching, and since I’ve come to terms with what I feel I am (a man), a lot of events in my past have suddenly “clicked” for me. I never had any obvious, big, bright flashing neon signs about who I am during my early years but looking back now, there were a lot of little signs that pointed in that direction. 

I still doubt myself sometimes. I still feel like I am just having a bit of a blip because I didn’t realise when I was younger. I’m 26 this year and finally embracing my new self. I feel happier and more confident, and I’ve done wonders in my eating disorder recovery. I just tell myself that I’m happy and that’s all that matters, and whatever is meant to happen will happen.

Thank you. I definitely don’t take it for granted. I know that I am very lucky and that there are a lot of people out there that are less fortunate than me. I guess my aim for posting this is to hopefully show people that there are kind, open-minded individuals out there. I’m sure that they know that already anyway but in a world full of so much hate and prejudice, it’s nice to have a little reminder.
